Ren, 18 October 2026, choosing among the options the AI offered: "Renames, full scope" ([source](../../../../../../sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-17-registration-dualist-vocabulary.md#rens-decision-on-the-renaming-18-october-2026)). What changed, the departures from what was offered and what was left are in the [naming study](../../REGISTRATION-VOCABULARY-STUDY.md#8-applied-n5-18-october-2026). The full table is [RENAME-TABLE.json](../../../history/root-foundation/development/n1-migration/RENAME-TABLE.json).
- The renaming was applied by [apply_renames.py](../../../history/root-foundation/development/n1-migration/apply_renames.py) on a branch. It separates Lean code from comments: identifiers are renamed in code and inside backticks; prose words are left alone. Short common names (`record`, `learner`, `Holds`, `registered`) are renamed bare only in the files whose namespaces they belong to.
- Both checker runs passed with no fix needed after the rewrite.
- FallibleInquiry, a periphery with its own checker, was rechecked (`check_fallible_inquiry.py`, receipt `20261018T063731.167536Z`, 31 theorems), and its three records were bound to that receipt.
- [rebind_records.py](../../../history/root-foundation/development/n1-migration/rebind_records.py) rewrote the records' live fields (not `history` or `text_versions`) and rehashed every reference to a changed file. It rebound every proof binding to a changed Lean file to the receipt, and added a history note to each record it changed.
